northStar: An original premium 1994-1997 arcade and DOS giant-machine fighter: strong held-cel posing, mechanically coherent Frames, expressive 1990s cel-illustrated Pilots, severe corporate-industrial stages and hard readable broadcast UI.
historicalReferenceLessons: learn pilot-plus-machine identity and tournament consequence from 1990s PC robot fighters without copying any commercial robot or screen
learn silhouette, anticipation, hero-contact, recovery, portrait hierarchy and super readability from top 1990s Japanese arcade fighters without reproducing their characters, poses or layouts
learn industrial serviceability, access panels, load paths and believable machine scale from 1990s grounded mecha design
learn corporate infrastructure, rain, telecommunications and human vulnerability from 1990s cyberpunk animation
learn decisive contact weight and intimidation from 1990s 3D fighting presentation while keeping final gameplay fully authored 2D sprites

pixelGrammar.clusterRule: deliberate connected pixel clusters at native size; no resampled fuzz
pixelGrammar.outlineRule: selective dark contour clusters and joint cavities; avoid uniform comic outlines on every internal edge
pixelGrammar.antiAliasRule: no global antialiasing; only intentional hand-placed transition pixels where the approved native style requires them
pixelGrammar.materialRule: major metal families use shadow, base, light, hard highlight and restrained specular accents rather than smooth PBR gradients
pixelGrammar.lightingRule: stable upper-front gameplay key light; arena colour may influence selected highlights but may not redraw material identity

frameDesignGrammar: every Frame must answer cockpit, crew, power, recoil, cooling and service-access logic before decoration
head, shoulder, forearm, torso, pelvis, lower-leg and foot silhouettes must remain independently recognisable
hardpoints and moving panels must attach to declared mechanical landmarks
signature asymmetry must be documented before animation and explicitly reviewed after runtime mirroring
weapon reach must come from declared mechanisms rather than arbitrary limb stretching
effects never replace a readable physical body pose
pilotDesignGrammar: Pilots use strong 1990s cel-animation face shapes, two dominant shadow bands and decisive expression changes
clothing begins with occupation, corporation and cockpit function rather than generic tactical decoration
hair mass, face proportions, scars, collars and signature accessories are identity landmarks and cannot drift between portraits
super cut-ins are three held cels, not miniature modern cinematics
all generated typography is prohibited; names and move text are separately authored bitmap assets

animationGrammar.principle: few excellent drawings held deliberately are preferred to smooth filler

frameCadence.bastion: heavy-held hydraulic load and late recovery
frameCadence.viper: fast-snap compression and hard mechanical brake
frameCadence.mirage: precise physical body with independently timed false-vector effects

forbidden: smooth skeletal tweening used as final character animation
crawling panel detail from cel to cel
effect clouds used to hide weak attack silhouettes

uiGrammar: 640x360-first hard pixel composition with hierarchy before decoration
health, timer, rounds, guard and CORE read before ornamental telemetry
menus use hard latches, stepped wipes and restrained low-rate animation rather than spring easing or glass panels
Pilot select prioritises portrait personality; Frame select prioritises silhouette, crew, CORE and combat doctrine
title and move typography are hand-authored assets, never provider text
environmentGrammar: every arena has a clean horizontal fight plane and clear far, mid, play-plane and foreground value separation
service ladders, cranes, vents, cable routes and containment infrastructure must have believable purpose
ambient loops stay low-rate and may not compete with fighter silhouettes
rain, steam, sparks and smoke are sparse stepped cels or separate effects, not low-alpha particle soup
